inspiration: Data-driven terrain rules (DATA FIRST: module/Ultima-IV/config.b line 132). Each terrain row sets walk, swim and sail flags, a speed class, and an optional status effect. One example slows and poisons; another is a slow-walk terrain. This is the shape to copy for zone-as-data (row 20 and 21) and terrain speed modifiers. Fit: row 21 catalogue fields.

Encounter groups on each creature row (config.b line 48 onward; line 73 has an encounter size of one for a sea vessel). Each row also carries a movement mode (fixed or wandering), whether it can step onto the player, and whether it refuses to attack. Shape for spawn data (row 23): size, movement mode, and attack flags kept as data fields.

Force-of-nature hazards: two roaming entries (config.b lines 80-81, a whirlpool and a twister). Their rows set wandering movement, a not-attack flag, and can-move-onto-avatar; the engine's attackability test is creature.cpp line 54 (it checks a non-attackable attribute; the mapping from these row flags was not read). Reads as weather, not an enemy. Idea for a telegraphed roaming hazard in a zone (vfx and threat readability).

Three named cast cues: precast, flash, and fizzle (module/Ultima-IV/sound/spell_precast_dos.ogg, spell_flash_dos.ogg, fizzle.rfx). Roles are inferred from the file names; the audio was not played. Fit for specials (row 13) and sound cues (row 12).

Context-named music (module/Ultima-IV/music/minstrel/). One bed per place or state: towns, castles, dungeons, shrines, merchants, combat, and a fanfare stinger. Fit for music layering by biome and border crossfades (sound-music topic).

Shadowcasting from occluder shapes. The GPU path accepts occluder shapes and a shadowcast shader (src/gpu_opengl.cpp line 1514; module/render/shader/shadowcast.glsl). Idea for 2D line-of-sight vision in dark zones or the Pit (camera, vfx).

Level-indexed dungeon dressing: wall and door sets per depth (module/Ultima-IV/image/ega/dung0ma.png, dung1ma_door.png, dung3ma_door.png, dungeonhall_door.png). Numbered sets 0 to 3 (depth inferred from the names). Idea for zone dressing variants (zones topic).

briefs.label: Roaming storm ring
briefs.why: A hazard that drifts through the arena reads as weather, so players dodge it instead of fighting it. Silhouette is a ring that is readable at 375 wide.
briefs.keep: The hazard roams on its own path, is data-driven (wandering movement, a not-attack flag, can move onto the avatar), and can carry the player off line.
briefs.change: Give it a telegraphed spinning ring with a ground shadow and a slow tick sound instead of a sprite swap; use a different hazard type (not water). Keep Dom's rule: an original storm, not the donor's sprite or sound.
briefs.ref: module/Ultima-IV/config.b lines 80-81 (creature rows, names not copied here)

briefs.label: Mire slows and stings
briefs.why: A terrain that slows and adds a damage-over-time status makes route choice a real decision, and the status is visible on the feet.
briefs.keep: One terrain row carries both a speed class and a status effect, so the terrain is data, not code.
briefs.change: Show the poison as a green ring on the feet and a short drip sound, not text; use a different terrain name and palette. Keep Dom's rule: recreate as our own mire, not the donor's swamp.

briefs.label: Three-beat cast cue
briefs.why: Three distinct cast sounds (start, hit, fizzle) make the cast readable without a HUD, which matters at 375 wide.
briefs.keep: Separate audio for the cast start, a flash, and a failed cast (roles inferred from the file names).
briefs.change: Choose length and pitch by spell school; add a visual tell for the failed cast. Keep Dom's rule: our own sounds, never the donor's files.

briefs.label: Depth-keyed dressing
briefs.why: Depth read by the art set lets players know the zone level without a label.
briefs.keep: One dressing set per depth, selected by a level index.
briefs.change: Use one tile set with a colour band per depth rather than separate art sets; change the band colour, not the wall shape. Keep Dom's rule: distinct original tiles.
